extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and programmers using PARI for polynomial, p-adic, and power-series computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions operating on integers, polynomials, power series and p-adic objects; includes function semantics, parameter meanings, algorithmic notes, warnings and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: znprimroot
rubrics_metrics.description: Library function to obtain a primitive root of (Z/nZ) or related generator information: library syntax is GEN znprimroot(GEN n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as available in the library; determining exact orders may require factoring p-1 for large p which may be costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: znstar(n, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the structure of the multiplicative group (Z/nZ)*. For flag=0 returns an abelian group structure [h, d, g] where h = φ(n), d is vector of cyclic component orders di (di>1, di | di-1) and g gives generators; for flag=1 returns a bid structure enabling discrete logarithm computations (znlog).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given for znstar(40) showing G.no, G.cyc and G.gen; special-case: znstar(0) defined as [2,[2],[-1]] corresponding to Z* (flag=1 not implemented in that trivial case). Library syntax: GEN znstar0(GEN n, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: O(p^e) / zeropadic / zeroser
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs zero with specified p-adic or X-adic precision: if p is integer > 2 returns a p-adic 0 of precision e; otherwise returns a power series zero with precision given by ev where v is the X-adic valuation of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntaxes: GEN ggrando(); GEN zeropadic(GEN p, long e) for p-adic; GEN zeroser(long v, long e) for a power-series zero in variable v.

rubrics_metrics.name: bezoutres (deprecated alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for polresultantext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use polresultantext0 / polresultantext instead; library syntax provided: GEN polresultantext0(GEN A, GEN B, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: deriv(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivative of x with respect to main variable (or v if provided). Derivative of a scalar is zero; derivative of vector/matrix is componentwise. Shortcut x' may be used for derivative wrt main variable of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_POLMOD, the main variable is the main variable among coefficients of representative and modulus; derivative taken with respect to main variable used in base ring R. Library syntax: GEN deriv(GEN x, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: diffop(x, v, d, {n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies n-th power of a differential operator D to x, where v is a vector of variables and d is a vector giving D(v[i]) = d[i]. Scalars map to zero; applied componentwise to vectors/matrices. For t_POLMOD, missing modulus-variable value may be derived using implicit function theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can differentiate formal expressions; examples given (derivative of exp(X^2), differentiating Sin/Cos under relation Sin^2+Cos^2=1 with Cos' = -Sin); used to compute Bell polynomials via Faa di Bruno. Library syntax: GEN diffop0(GEN x, GEN v, GEN d, long n) and GEN diffop(GEN x, GEN v, GEN d) for n=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: eval(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace formal variables in x by values assigned after creation; for strings, execute as GP command and return its output. Useful mainly in GP interactive mode (not library mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show evaluating constructed strings and executing function calls; syntax errors raise e_SYNTAX which can be trapped; library syntax: GEN geval(GEN x). Note: do not confuse with substitution (subst).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorpadic(pol, p, r)
rubrics_metrics.description: p-adic factorization of polynomial pol to precision r, returning two-column matrix of factors as in factor. This is approximation of true factorization in Q_p[X], not factorization over Z/p^rZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors normalized so leading coefficient is a power of p. Method: modified version of Zassenhaus round-4. If polynomial has inexact t_PADIC coefficients, the polynomial is first made integral and lifted to Z (truncate coefficientwise), so one actually factors an exact polynomial p-adically close to input. Advice: prefer exact rational coefficients to avoid pitfalls. Library syntax: factorpadic(GEN f, GEN p, long r) (factorpadic0 deprecated). Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intformal(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal (symbolic) integral of x with respect to variable v (main variable if omitted). PARI cannot represent logarithmic or arctangent terms; presence yields an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument x can be any type; for rational functions base ring assumed to be integral domain of characteristic zero. For t_POLMOD main variable defined as for deriv; integrating with respect to main variable of x.mod is meaningless and raises error. Library syntax: GEN integ(GEN x, long v = -1). Examples and error case shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: padicappr(pol, a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of p-adic roots of polynomial pol congruent to p-adic number a modulo p, with same p-adic precision as a. a may be t_PADIC or an integral element of finite extension given as t_POLMOD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a is t_POLMOD in extension, result is vector of roots in same extension. Library syntax: GEN padicappr(GEN pol, GEN a). Also available GEN Zp_appr(GEN f, GEN a) when a is t_PADIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: padicfields(p, N, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a vector of polynomials generating all extensions of degree N of Q_p. N may be [n,d] to return extensions of degree n and discriminant p^d. The list is minimal (polynomials generate non-isomorphic extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If P in list and α a root, then α is sum of uniformizer and a lift of generator of residue field and powers of α generate ring of p-adic integers of K. flag=1 replaces P by [P,e,f,d,c] with ramification index e, residue degree f, discriminant valuation d, number of conjugate fields c. flag=2 returns number of extensions using Krasner's formula (fast). Library syntaxes: GEN padicfields0(GEN p, GEN N, long flag) and GEN padicfields(GEN p, long n, long d, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: polchebyshev(n, {flag = 1}, {a = 'x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns nth Chebyshev polynomial of first kind T_n (flag=1) or second kind U_n (flag=2), evaluated at a (x by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polynomials satisfy 3-term recurrence P_{n+1} = 2x P_n - P_{n-1} with initial conditions U0=T0=1, T1=x, U1=2x. Relations: T_n(cos z)=cos(nz), U_{n-1}(cos z)=sin(nz)/sin z, T_n = n U_{n-1}. Definitions for n<0 and special values noted. Library syntaxes: GEN polchebyshev_eval(long n, long flag, GEN a = NULL), GEN polchebyshev(long n, long v), GEN polchebyshev1 and polchebyshev2 for T_n and U_n respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: polclass(D, {inv = 0}, {x = 'x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a polynomial in Z[x] generating the Hilbert class field for imaginary quadratic discriminant D. If inv=0 uses modular j-function (classical Hilbert polynomial), otherwise uses a class invariant specified by inv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of allowed invariants inv and congruence conditions on D are provided (many specific inv values require D ≡ 1 mod 8, D ≡ 1,2 mod 3, or other congruences). For double eta quotients w_{p,q} extra technical conditions ensure full Hilbert class field generation (non-inert, prime to conductor, class-group constraints). Algorithm: uses Chinese remaindering modulo small primes (no floating-point complex evaluation), so class invariant may be any of several algebraic roots of modular polynomial—returned class invariant may correspond to different algebraic conjugates and precise root identification not asserted. Examples shown; library syntax: GEN polclass(GEN D, long inv, long x = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcoef(x, n, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Coefficient of degree n of polynomial x with respect to main variable (or v). If n > degree, returns 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to scalars (degree 0), rational functions with monomial denominators, and power series (if n less than valuation returns 0). If n greater than largest significant degree for power series, an error is issued. Library syntax: GEN polcoef(GEN x, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcoeff (deprecated alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for polcoef.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polcoeff0(GEN x, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcyclo(n, {a = 'x})
rubrics_metrics.description: nth cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at a (x by default). n must be positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: reduce to squarefree n, use Φ_{np}(x)=Φ_n(x^p)/Φ_n(x) and product formula Φ_n(x)=∏_{d|n}(x^d−1)^{μ(n/d)}. In evaluated case algorithm assumes a^d - 1 is either 0 or invertible for all d|n; if base ring has zero divisors use subst(polcyclo(n),x,a). Library syntaxes: GEN polcyclo_eval(long n, GEN a = NULL), GEN polcyclo(long n, long v).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcyclofactors(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of polynomials whose product is the product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials dividing f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting polynomials may themselves be products of cyclotomic polynomials and not irreducible. Examples show factorization and checking with poliscyclo/poliscycloprod. Library syntax: GEN polcyclofactors(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldegree(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of polynomial x in main variable (or v). Degree(0) is -oo; degree of non-zero scalar is 0; for non-zero polynomial/rational returns ordinary degree. Raises error otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntaxes: GEN gppoldegree(GEN x, long v = -1) and long poldegree(GEN x, long v) (returns -LONG_MAX if x=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldisc(pol, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of polynomial pol in main variable (or v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses modular algorithm over Z or Q, and subresultant algorithm otherwise. Applies also to types t_QUAD and t_QFI/t_QFR (shown examples). Library syntax: GEN poldisc0(GEN pol, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldiscfactors(T, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given polynomial T with integer coefficients, return [D, faD] where D is discriminant and faD a partial factorization: first-column entries are coprime and not perfect powers but need not be primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 finish factorization using factorint. Examples show partial factorization and effect of flag=1. Library syntax: GEN poldiscfactors(GEN T, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldiscreduced(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced discriminant vector of integral, monic polynomial f: vector of elementary divisors of Z[α]/f(α)Z[α], components positive and product equals absolute discriminant of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN reduceddiscsmith(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: polgraeffe(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns Graeffe transform g of f such that g(x^2) = f(x) f(-x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polgraeffe(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: polhensellift(A, B, p, e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifts a factorization modulo p to modulo p^e: given prime p, integral polynomial A with leading coefficient a p-unit, and B a vector of monic polynomials pairwise relatively prime modulo p whose product ≡ A/lc(A) mod p, return lifted factors modulo p^e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalization: if T irreducible mod p and B is factorization of A over F_p[t]/(T), replace p by [p,T] to lift to Z_p[t]/(T, p^e). Example given that includes lifting with T = t^3-2, p=7 and shows verifying lifted product modulo p^6. Library syntax: GEN polhensellift(GEN A, GEN B, GEN p, long e).

rubrics_metrics.name: polhermite(n, {a = 'x})
rubrics_metrics.description: nth Hermite polynomial H_n evaluated at a (x by default), defined by H_n(x) = (-1)^n e^{x^2} d^n/dx^n e^{-x^2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polhermite_eval(long n, GEN a = NULL) and GEN polhermite(long n, long v) to return polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: polinterpolate(X, {Y}, {t = 'x}, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given data vectors X and optional Y (same length), finds interpolating polynomial P of minimal degree passing through points and evaluates at t. If Y omitted uses (i, X[i]). Optional e will contain an error estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polint(GEN X, GEN Y = NULL, GEN t = NULL, GEN *e = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: poliscyclo(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 0 if f is not a cyclotomic polynomial; returns n > 0 if f = Φ_n (n-th cyclotomic polynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: poliscyclo(x^4-x^2+1) = 12; polcyclo(12) returns polynomial. Library syntax: long poliscyclo(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: poliscycloprod(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 1 if f is a product of cyclotomic polynomials, and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show using factor and poliscyclo to check factors. Library syntax: long poliscycloprod(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: polisirreducible(pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 if pol is non-constant and irreducible; 0 otherwise. Irreducibility checked over the smallest base field over which pol seems defined (univariate in this version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long isirreducible(GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollead(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Leading coefficient of polynomial or power series x with respect to main variable (or v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN pollead(GEN x, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollegendre(n, {a = 'x})
rubrics_metrics.description: nth Legendre polynomial evaluated at a (x by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN pollegendre_eval(long n, GEN a = NULL) and GEN pollegendre(long n, long v).

rubrics_metrics.name: polmodular(L, {inv = 0}, {x = NULL}, {y = 'x}, {derivs = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return modular polynomial of prime level L in variables x and y for modular function specified by inv (0=j, 1=Weber f, 5=γ2=j^{1/3}, etc.). If x is Mod(j,p) or element j of finite field evaluate polynomial at j. If j from finite field and derivs non-zero return triple [poly evaluated, first derivative, second derivative].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See polclass for list of invariants. Examples show explicit polynomials and evaluation in finite fields. Library syntax: GEN polmodular(long L, long inv, GEN x = NULL, long y = -1, long derivs).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrecip(pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal polynomial of pol: coefficients reversed. pol must be a polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polrecip(GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: polresultant(x, y, {v}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Resultant of two polynomials x and y with respect to main variables (or v). Assumes base ring is a domain. For u and v such that x*u + y*v = Res(x,y) use polresultantext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0 (default) choose best algorithm: subresultant (Lazard/Ducos) in generic case, modular algorithm for Q[X], or Sylvester's matrix for inexact inputs. If flag=1 use Sylvester determinant. If x or y are multivariate with huge polynomial content, remove content manually to speed up—function does not remove content automatically because it may be expensive. Example demonstrates content removal trick. Library syntax: GEN polresultant0(GEN x, GEN y, long v = -1, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: polresultantext(A, B, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Find polynomials U and V such that A*U + B*V = R where R is the resultant of A and B with respect to main variables (or v). Returns [U, V, R].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: subresultant assuming base ring is a domain. Examples illustrate returned U, V, R and verification. Library syntax: GEN polresultantext0(GEN A, GEN B, long v = -1) and GEN polresultantext(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: polroots(T)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute complex roots of polynomial T as column vector repeating roots according to multiplicity. Precision in GP is controlled by realprecision; in library must provide precision argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: modification of Schönhage's root-finding algorithm implemented by Gourdon; guaranteed to converge and for rational-coefficient polynomials roots are accurate to required relative accuracy. Library syntax: GEN roots(GEN T, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsbound(T, {tau = 0.01})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a sharp upper bound B for modulus of largest complex root of T with relative error τ: |z| ≤ B for all roots and exists a root with |z0| ≥ B exp(-2τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much faster than polroots/polrootsreal; examples show timings and effect of setting tau to allow looser bounds (factor 2). Library syntax: GEN polrootsbound(GEN T, GEN tau = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsff (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete; kept for backward compatibility. Use factormod instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polrootsff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsmod(f, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of roots of polynomial f over finite field defined by domain D. D may be a prime p (factor over F_p), [T,p] for extension modulus T over F_p, a t_FFELT field element, or omitted (factor over field of definition of f which must be finite field). Multiple roots are not repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: factoring mod 2, mod 3, mod extension [3,y^2+1], working with field elements and lifting. Library syntax: GEN polrootsmod(GEN f, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootspadic(x, p, r)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of p-adic roots of polynomial x to p-adic precision r (p prime). Multiple roots not repeated. These are approximations in Z/p^rZ of true roots in Q_p, not roots in Z/p^rZ per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If polynomial has inexact t_PADIC coefficients, polynomial is made integral by dividing out p-adic content then lifted to Z via truncate coefficientwise; thus roots approximate roots of exact polynomial close p-adically. Advice: factor polynomials with exact rational coefficients to avoid pitfalls. Library syntax: GEN rootpadic(GEN x, GEN p, long r). Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsreal(T, {ab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Real roots of real-coefficient polynomial T returned with multiplicities, to relative accuracy realprecision. If ab provided, restrict to closed interval [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coefficients/range are exact (avoid t_REALs) algorithm is guaranteed (Uspensky's method with Descartes' rule, Rouillier & Zimmerman). If rescaling/rounding used for non-rational coefficients result may be wrong. Special handling if T = Q(x^h) when ab omitted: routine applies to Q and takes h-th roots appropriately; if ab present it will not change variables automatically. Library syntax: GEN realroots(GEN T, GEN ab = NULL, long prec). Examples and remarks included.

rubrics_metrics.name: polsturm(T, {ab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of distinct real roots of real polynomial T; if ab provided restrict to [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer exact inputs (no t_REAL) for guaranteed result using Uspensky method; inexact inputs are first rescaled and rounded and may give wrong result. If only one endpoint is inexact the interval is thickened using rational endpoints and result remains guaranteed unless a root is very close to a non-rational endpoint. Note: if polynomial not squarefree roots are not repeated. Library syntaxes: long RgX_sturmpart(GEN T, GEN ab) or long sturm(GEN T) for ab=NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: polsubcyclo(n, d, {v = 'x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives polynomials (in variable v) defining sub-abelian extensions of degree d of cyclotomic field Q(ζ_n) where d | φ(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exactly one such extension output is polynomial; otherwise vector of polynomials (possibly empty). Use concat([], polsubcyclo(n,d)) to ensure vector output. Use galoissubcyclo to specify which sub-Abelian extension to compute. Library syntax: GEN polsubcyclo(long n, long d, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsylvestermatrix(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Sylvester matrix corresponding to polynomials x and y with coefficients placed in columns (natural for solving equations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for polynomials with inexact entries since polynomial Euclidean division is ill-suited to inexact coefficients. Library syntax: GEN sylvestermatrix(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsym(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates column vector of symmetric powers of roots of polynomial x up to power n using Newton's formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polsym(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: poltchebi (deprecated alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for polchebyshev.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polchebyshev1(long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polzagier(n, m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates Zagier's polynomial P_n^{(m)} used in convergence acceleration functions sumalt and sumpos (with flag=1). If m<0 or m≥n polynomial is zero. For n>m>0, P_n^{(m)} relates to Legendre polynomials and difference sequences with step 2; further formula provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: Cohen et al., 'Convergence acceleration of alternating series', Exper. Math., 2000. Library syntax: GEN polzag(long n, long m).

rubrics_metrics.name: serconvol(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convolution (Hadamard product) of two power series x and y: if x = Σ a_k X^k and y = Σ b_k X^k then result is Σ (a_k * b_k) X^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN convol(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: serlaplace(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given power series x with non-negative exponents or a polynomial, if x = Σ (a_k/k!) X^k then serlaplace(x) = Σ a_k X^k (Laplace transform-like map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN laplace(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: serreverse(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse power series of s: the series t such that t(s) = x; requires s valuation exactly 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: serreverse(tan(x)) returns series for arctan; verify tan(t) = x + O(x^n). Library syntax: GEN serreverse(GEN s).

rubrics_metrics.name: subst(x, y, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace simple variable y by argument z in expression x. Works on all types; for non-polynomial x substitution treats scalar components as polynomials of degree zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveats: substituting scalar 1 by a non-square matrix raises 'forbidden substitution by a non square matrix' error; if x is a power series z must be polynomial/power series/rational function; substitution applied entrywise for vectors/matrices/lists. Use substvec for multiple variables and substpol for polynomial-substitutions. Library syntax: GEN gsubst(GEN x, long y, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: substpol(x, y, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace 'variable' y (which may be any polynomial) by z in polynomial expression x. The substitution is done by moding out components by y−t where t is new free variable, then substituting t by z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different outcomes depending on y being x^2, x^3 or (x+1)^2. Additional helper gdeflate(GEN T, long v, long d) attempts to write T(x) in form t(x^d) and returns NULL on failure. Library syntax: GEN gsubstpol(GEN x, GEN y, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: substvec(x, v, w)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneously replace vector v of monomials (degree 1 variables) by expressions w of same length in x. Substitutions done simultaneously (vi replaced by new variables then new variables replaced by wi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show simultaneous substitution behavior (avoid sequential semantics). Library syntax: GEN gsubstvec(GEN x, GEN v, GEN w).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumformal(f, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal sum of polynomial expression f with respect to main variable (or v). Returns polynomial F in v vanishing at 0 such that F(b)-F(a) = Σ_{v=a+1}^b f(v). Base ring assumed characteristic zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show summing polynomials, verifying substitution yields correct finite sums. Library syntax: GEN sumformal(GEN f, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: taylor(x, t, {d = seriesprecision})
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor expansion around 0 of x with respect to simple variable t to order d. x can be many types; function adds O(t^d) to components unlike Ser which considers valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows taylor(x/(1+y), y, 5) and contrast with Ser which requires main-variable higher priority. Library syntax: GEN tayl(GEN x, long t, long precdl).

rubrics_metrics.name: thue(tnf, a, {sol})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return all integer solutions (x,y) of Thue equation P(x,y)=a where tnf is produced by thueinit(P). If sol provided it must contain solutions of Norm(x)=a modulo units of positive norm as computed by bnfisintnorm. If infinitely many solutions exist an error is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed to input polynomial P directly (thue will call thueinit(P,0) but this is wasteful if many queries). If tnf computed without assuming GRH result is unconditional; otherwise result may be conditional on GRH in principle, but may still be unconditionally correct in favorable cases. The documentation lists conditionality criteria when a ≠ ±1 and P has single irreducible rational factor: tentative class number h > 1 and R/0.2 > 1.5, where R is regulator computed assuming GRH. Examples show unconditional and conditional cases and how to check K.no and K.reg from bnfinit.
